definition: to carefully consider a situation, person or problem in order to make a judgment
examples: We tried to assess his suitability for the job.

definition: to calculate what something costs or is worth
examples: Our agent will assess the value of your property.

definition: to believe that something is true, even though no one has told you or even though you have no proof
examples: Everyone accepted she was telling the truth, although in fact this was quite a lot to assume.

definition: if a problem, someone's behaviour, etc baffles you, you cannot understand it or solve it
examples: Detectives remain baffled by these murders.

definition: preferring one person, thing or idea to another in a way that is unfair
examples: It was a biased report.

definition: to have a particular opinion about someone or something
examples: They consider it inevitable that some jobs will be lost.

definition: to consider doing something in the future
examples: I'm contemplating retirement next year.

definition: to think very carefully about something for a long time
examples: I haven't got time to sit around contemplating the meaning of life.

definition: someone who is cynical believes that people care only about themselves and are not sincere or honest, or expects things not to be successful or useful
examples: I know that some of you are very cynical about the proposals.

definition: to know something as a result of considering the information or evidence that you have
examples: Finding fossils far inland, he deduced that the area had once been covered by water.

definition: to think about or discuss something very carefully, especially before you make an important decision
examples: The judges deliberated for an hour before choosing the winner.

definition: a situation in which you have to make a difficult decision
examples: I'm in a dilemma over whether to tell him or not.

definition: to treat someone unfairly because of their religion, race or other personal features
examples: Employers are not allowed to discriminate on the basis of gender.

definition: to recognise the difference between things
examples: Long-range missile attacks simply cannot discriminate between military and civilian targets.

definition: not completely good, safe or honest
examples: The story seemed a bit dubious to me.

definition: not sure about the truth or quality of something, or whether you should do something
examples: I'm very dubious about his ability to do the job.

definition: an amount that you guess or calculate using the information available
examples: According to official estimates, over 25% of carbon emissions come from the United States.

definition: a statement telling a customer how much money you will charge if they employ you to do a particular piece of work
examples: The committee are currently getting estimates for repairs to the stonework.

definition: to say what you think an amount or value will be, either by guessing or by using available information to calculate it
examples: It's difficult to estimate the cost of making your house safe.

definition: strong belief in or trust of someone or something
examples: I'm delighted to know you have such faith in me.

definition: to believe that something is true, although no one has directly told you about it
examples: You're new here, I gather.
